issues.description: Duplicate 'transcriber_error' entry in error message_type tuple
issues.detail: In the new error handling tuple, 'transcriber_error' appears twice (lines ~728 and ~733 of the new code). This is a copy-paste bug that has no functional impact (tuple membership is unaffected) but signals incomplete review and risks masking an intended-but-missing error type the author meant to include. The author should diff this against the ElevenLabs cookbook list and confirm whether one occurrence was supposed to be a different error type.

issues.description: Removed exception handler may surface noisy disconnect tracebacks instead of a clean warning
issues.detail: Previously, _receive_messages wrapped _process_messages in try/except and logged a warning when the websocket connection closed. The diff removes the outer try/except entirely. While this is necessary to break the infinite-reconnect loop (the stated fix), it means a normal websocket close (ConnectionClosed, etc.) will now propagate as an exception up to the websocket_service reconnect loop without the previous friendly warning. Consider adding a narrowly-scoped except for websockets.ConnectionClosed that logs a warning and then re-raises, so observability is preserved without re-introducing the swallow-and-loop bug.

issues.description: Inner try/except around message processing still swallows all exceptions
issues.detail: The inner 'except Exception as e: logger.error(...)' inside the async for loop still catches every exception type, including programming errors (KeyError, AttributeError) from _process_response. This means malformed-but-parseable messages will be logged and silently skipped indefinitely. At minimum, the bare 'except Exception' should be narrowed, or the error path should consider pushing an ErrorFrame so downstream consumers know processing degraded.

issues.description: Error frame loses message_type discrimination that callers may want
issues.detail: Previously each error type ('error', 'auth_error', 'quota_exceeded_error') produced a distinct prefix ('Error:', 'Auth error:', 'Quota exceeded:') in push_error. The collapsed branch now uses only 'Error: <error>' (or 'Error: Unknown error - <message_type>' when data lacks 'error'). Downstream pipelines that key off the prefix to distinguish auth/quota from generic errors will silently lose that signal. Consider including message_type in the pushed error string unconditionally, e.g. f'{message_type}: {error_msg}'.

issues.description: Per-error logger.error() call removed; only push_error is called
issues.detail: The prior code logged each error via logger.error before pushing the frame. The new code does not call logger.error at all for the consolidated error branch; it relies entirely on push_error to surface the issue. If push_error does not log (or logs at a lower level), operators will lose visibility on auth/quota errors in logs. Verify push_error's behavior or restore an explicit logger.error.

changelog/3233.fixed.md ends without a trailing newline ('\ No newline at end of file'). Minor style/POSIX-compliance issue; some changelog aggregators concatenate files and rely on trailing newlines to separate entries.

issues.description: Dead comment left behind after method consolidation
issues.detail: The line '# Connection closed, will reconnect on next audio chunk' is preserved at the new end of _receive_messages, but the surrounding code that actually handled connection-closed (the outer except) has been removed. The comment now sits unmoored and arguably contradicts the new behavior (which is to let the exception propagate to the reconnect loop in websocket_service). Either remove the comment or move it to where reconnect actually happens.

issues.description: No test coverage added for the fix
issues.detail: The PR fixes a 'whole process blocks' bug — exactly the kind of regression that warrants a regression test. There is no test added that exercises the disconnect path and asserts that _receive_messages raises rather than loops. Hard to prevent re-regression without one.

dissents.topic: Whether to keep any try/except around the receive loop

positions.position: Removing the outer try/except is the simplest, smallest fix that demonstrably breaks the infinite loop. Re-introducing exception handling risks re-introducing the bug. Ship as-is.

A narrowly-scoped except for websockets.ConnectionClosed that logs a warning and re-raises preserves the prior log message without swallowing the exception. The current diff over-corrects by removing all locally-scoped diagnostics.

dissents.topic: Collapsing per-error-type branches into a tuple

positions.position: The tuple consolidation is correct DRY: 11 error types with identical handling don't need 11 elif branches. The prefix differentiation was incidental complexity.

Auth, quota, and generic errors have semantically different downstream implications (retry vs. fail-fast vs. backoff). Collapsing them with a uniform 'Error:' prefix loses information that downstream stages legitimately needed. The fix should preserve message_type in the pushed error.
Tuple membership is unaffected by duplicates; this is purely cosmetic and can be fixed in a follow-up.

A duplicate strongly implies the author intended a different error type (e.g. 'transcriber_warning' or a typo) and the actual list of handled errors may be incomplete relative to the ElevenLabs cookbook. Worth blocking on a quick re-check before merge.

review.summary: The PR makes two correct intent-level changes: (1) removing the outer try/except in _receive_messages so websocket disconnects propagate to the reconnect loop instead of being swallowed into an infinite loop, and (2) expanding the set of recognized ElevenLabs error message types. Both are well-motivated and the infinite-loop fix in particular is load-bearing. However, execution has rough edges: 'transcriber_error' is duplicated in the tuple (suggesting a missed error type), per-error logger.error() calls were dropped in favor of relying on push_error, the distinct error prefixes were collapsed which may lose information downstream consumers depend on, and a dangling comment about reconnect remains in code that no longer handles reconnect locally. No regression test was added for the headline bug. Recommend addressing the duplicate, restoring per-message_type discrimination in the pushed error string, and either adding a narrow ConnectionClosed log or confirming push_error logs at error level before merge.
